clue.text: A miss from August and, with time, a miss from Will

parts.note: Miss Julie is the play by August Strindberg
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Two young women are traced to two men, one called August and one called Will.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'August' and 'Will' are playwrights: Strindberg wrote Miss Julie, and Will Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet. Add T for time to the first to get JULIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet is the young unmarried heroine Shakespeare created, so she is a maiden from Will's pen.

clue.text: One or the other litigated in 22 12 to preserve North Aberdeen airport

definitions.text: One or the other litigated in 22 12

parts.note: to jar is to preserve food in jars
N is the compass abbreviation for north
Aberdeen's airport is at Dyce

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is fought to save an airport in Scotland's north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 12 is BLEAK HOUSE, Dickens's novel, whose endless lawsuit is Jarndyce and Jarndyce: either party bears the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In the case Jarndyce and Jarndyce both sides share one surname, so either litigant in Dickens's novel is a Jarndyce.

clue.text: Blair ignoring Tyneside to hold service in Cyprus

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other
ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: Lionel Blair was a British dancer and television entertainer
Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A politician skips a north-east visit in order to attend church on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' looks like Tony the prime minister, but it is Lionel Blair, a British song-and-dance showman.
explanation.definitionFit: Limassol is a major port city on the south coast of Cyprus, so it is a place found on that island.

clue.text: Remove old oil refinery in some measure

definitions.note: the answer is an archaic word for remove, which 'old' signals

indicators.note: being in something means being placed inside it, so the refined letters go within the measure

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width

indicators.note: a refinery processes raw material into a new state, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Old oil is taken out of a refinery to a certain extent.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is half an em, a typesetting width.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloin is an obsolete legal word meaning to carry off or take away to a distance, so it is an old term for remove.

clue.text: Notables then, not-ables now?

parts.note: surface reading: people of note in the past who are no longer of note
setter's reading: split, the word means people who are not able any longer, faded celebrities whose time is past

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen turns 'notables' into 'not-ables': people who once counted and now no longer can.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose fame or usefulness belongs to the past, exactly the once-notable now forgotten.

clue.text: America's epistolist with a satiric look East, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters as one possible arrangement, inviting the solver to try another

parts.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An American letter-writer views the Orient with a mocking eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Alistair Cooke broadcast Letter from America on BBC radio for nearly sixty years, hence the epistolist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooke's long-running weekly radio talk was framed as a letter sent home from the United States, making him its letter-writer.

clue.text: One assuming the lead in "The Mousetrap"?

definitions.text: One assuming the lead in "The Mousetrap"?

parts.words: One assuming the lead in "The Mousetrap"
parts.note: surface reading: an actor playing the lead role in Agatha Christie's long-running play
setter's reading: a real mousetrap whose chief attraction is the bait, and an important person is called by that bait's name

explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is the Agatha Christie play that has run in London since 1952; read literally, the leading thing in a mousetrap is a lump of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is slang for an important, influential person, the one who leads, and cheese is what baits a mousetrap.

clue.text: Book the return passage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the second book of the Bible
second meaning: the departure of the Israelites from Egypt on the journey back to the promised land

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a request to reserve a ticket home; 'Book' is a noun, a volume of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The second Old Testament volume is named for the mass departure from Egypt, the journey that led the Israelites back toward Canaan.

clue.text: Donne's topped in a way by something of Petrarch's

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the shortened name goes inside the road

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: topped means having its head cut off, so the name loses its first letter

parts.note: John Donne the poet; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: One poet is outdone in some way by a work of another, Donne beaten by Petrarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne and Petrarch both wrote these fourteen-line poems, which hides the definition in plain sight; 'a way' is the usual crossword street.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrarch made the fourteen-line love poem famous, so a sonnet is the form most associated with him.

clue.text: "R loves me whole-heartedly!" (1 across)?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the heart of the whole is filled by a word, so one piece sits in the middle of the others

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scores, which looks like the letter O; two loves give two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Juliet exclaims happily that her beloved, known by his initial, adores her completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is something Juliet (1 across) might say of her lover: R, then ME at the heart of two loves, spells ROMEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is the lover of Juliet in Shakespeare's play, so he is the R she would say loves her.

clue.text: Cast aggressively before fish in fine feathers

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside the second phrase

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family
down is the soft fine plumage of birds

explanation.surface: An angler throws a line forcefully before landing a fish in a showy, well-dressed state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine feathers' looks like one phrase for finery; it splits into F and DOWN, with the fish placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling something down is to throw it hard to the ground, a forceful, hostile throw such as a challenge or gauntlet.

clue.text: Part of 9 and 1 across ravaging ie rural France

indicators.note: ravaging lays waste and wrecks, so these letters are torn apart and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something devastates the French countryside, as if an invading army were passing through.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 and 1 across are ROMEO and JULIET, so the play; a part is a role in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Laurence is the Franciscan who secretly marries the young lovers, a role in Shakespeare's tragedy Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Dethrone and sit on one dangerously

indicators.note: doing something dangerously is doing it wildly and recklessly, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rebel removes a monarch and then perches perilously on the vacated throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To disanoint is to undo a king's anointing, taking away the consecrated status that made him ruler, and so depose him.

clue.text: Accommodation with hot water in Yorkshire

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap
the Ouse is a river that flows through York

explanation.surface: An advert for lodgings in northern England boasts that hot water is supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the river through the city of York, in the English county of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a building where people live, so it provides lodging or a place to stay.

clue.text: Unravelling a logic, denser as compressed would you say?

indicators.note: something unravelling comes undone, so these letters are loosened and rewoven in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's argument comes apart and turns out thicker than it looked, as if squeezed tight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'compressed' is a loose way to put it: close-grained wood or stone has fine, tightly packed fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-grained material has its particles or fibres packed tightly together, which is how something squeezed into a dense mass looks.

clue.text: Fugitive with a record (Hear me out!) left

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: out here means out of place, so the words before it are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A runaway with a criminal record pleads to be heard before he left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fugitive' looks like a noun for a runaway; here it is the adjective meaning fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things last only a short time, and fugitive as an adjective means passing quickly away, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Wasted time after she didn't marry the writer

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the others, so the short one goes at the end

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman
a pen is what writes
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman regrets the years she frittered away after turning down an author's proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted time' looks like one phrase; split after 'Wasted', which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent describes something used foolishly or squandered, as in a misspent youth, the same as wasted.

clue.text: How oral evidence is presented, apparently

definitions.meaning: first meaning: spoken testimony is, literally, something voiced by a person
second meaning: a stock phrase for so people claim, introducing rumour

explanation.walkthrough: The comma separates two readings of one phrase: the literal manner of spoken testimony, and the hedge used for hearsay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces reported rumour, things people claim, and is a stock way of saying supposedly or reportedly.

clue.text: Subtle St Michael, the Destroyer

indicators.note: a destroyer wrecks things, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint is pictured as a cunning destroyer of evil, like the archangel slaying the dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle' is not an adjective here but a name: Subtle is the con-man title character of Ben Jonson's comedy The Alchemist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ben Jonson's play, the fraudster posing as a transmuter of metals is called Subtle, so his name identifies that role.

clue.text: Old Ford's highly placed houses

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British Ford saloon car of the 1950s to 1970s
second meaning: the band of twelve astrological signs in the sky, called houses by astrologers

explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Zodiac was a large British family saloon. Astrology divides the sky into twelve houses, which are high up in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was used for a discontinued British Ford model and for the celestial belt of twelve star-signs above us.

clue.text: Caribbean characters promoted in surrealist's festival

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it, so these letters go within the artist's name

parts.note: Salvador Dali, the surrealist painter

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, and in a down entry moving up reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies

explanation.surface: West Indian figures are given prominence at a celebration of a surrealist artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights held each autumn, so it is a religious celebration.

clue.text: Bad odour has the prince leaving the platform

indicators.note: a person leaving goes away, so that letter departs from the word it was in

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker
P is an abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: A prince stepping down from the stage leaves a nasty smell behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad odour' is meant in its figurative sense of disrepute, not a smell. Take P from PODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgrace, and to be in bad odour is the idiom for being out of favour.

clue.text: Forms of public transport by the Tiber, say

indicators.note: saying the phrase out loud is what matters, so its sound rather than its spelling is used

parts.note: the Tiber flows through Rome, so buses there are Rome buses

explanation.surface: A tourist note describes the kinds of public transport running along the river in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms' is the definition in its geometric sense: shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombuses are geometric shapes, parallelograms with four equal sides, so they are kinds of figure.

clue.text: Barren black betrayal

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
a leak is a betrayal of secret information

explanation.surface: A grim, desolate picture of dark treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleak landscape is bare, exposed and desolate, with nothing growing, the same as barren.

clue.text: Certain an assortment is sent?

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so these letters are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the an of an assortment is shared

explanation.surface: Someone is sure a mixed selection of goods has been dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' is the old slang for carried away with rapture, as in music that sends you.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sent by music is transported or enraptured, which is the dreamy, entranced state of being in a trance.

clue.text: Energy backing the last word in irrigation

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: something backing goes backwards, so the following phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: amen is the word that closes a prayer

explanation.surface: Power is behind the very latest development in watering technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word in irrigation' reads like 'the latest thing'; split it after 'word' and 'irrigation' is the definition in its medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is the medical flushing of the bowel with liquid, and irrigation is the clinical term for washing out a body cavity.

clue.text: They are hot and cold around the Southwark and Lambeth area

parts.note: a chill is a coldness

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the code is read from the end

parts.note: SE1 is the London postcode covering parts of Southwark and Lambeth; the digit 1 serves as the letter I

explanation.surface: Things that are hot and cold are found in a corner of south London.
explanation.walkthrough: SE1 is a London postal district on the south bank of the Thames; read backwards with the 1 as I it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chillies are pungent peppers whose heat burns the mouth, so they are things described as hot.

clue.text: Takes trouble with daughter? Cousins did!

indicators.note: trouble means disturbance, so these letters are disturbed into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family gathering: one relative goes to great lengths for a daughter, and the cousins did so too.
explanation.walkthrough: Cousins is Robin Cousins, the British figure skater who won Olympic gold in 1980, not relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Cousins was an Olympic champion figure skater, so what he did on the ice was glide on blades.
